# Generated by `swift run DiagnosticGoldenTool` — what WireOpenAPIGen answers each case with.
# `--check` fails if any of these stops firing or changes wording.

## route-scope/status-not-declared
# a mapped error is answered as one of the operation's own responses
rejected: Controller.swift:11: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound) on 'opA' maps to a status the document does not declare for it. It declares .ok. A mapped error is answered as one of the operation's own responses, so the document has to describe it — add it there, or map to one it already declares.

## route-scope/pair-form-against-a-bodied-response
# a bare case cannot construct a response the document gives a body
rejected: Controller.swift:11: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound) on 'opA' maps to a 404 response that carries a body, so a status alone cannot construct it. Supply one — @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound, { e in … }).

## route-scope/closure-form-against-a-bare-response
# a response carrying nothing has nowhere to put a body
rejected: Controller.swift:11: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound, …) on 'opA' supplies a body, but the document's 404 response carries none. Drop the closure.

## route-scope/terminal-scoped-pair-form-against-a-bodied-response
# a terminal-scoped mapping is exempt from naming a declared status, but not from the form of one the document does declare — it still gets a forwarder clause
rejected: Controller.swift:11: error: @ErrorResponse(DecodingError.self, .notFound) on 'opA' maps to a 404 response that carries a body, so a status alone cannot construct it. Supply one — @ErrorResponse(DecodingError.self, .notFound, { e in … }).

## route-scope/unconstructible-content-type
# the shim builds JSON bodies only
rejected: Controller.swift:11: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound) on 'opA' maps to a 404 response whose content type this adapter cannot construct — it builds JSON bodies only. Use @RawOperation for this operation.

## controller-scope/status-not-declared-for-some-operations
# a controller mapping covers every operation, so every one has to declare the status
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound) on 'GateController' maps to a status the document does not declare for 'opB'. A mapped error is answered as one of the operation's own responses, so every operation the mapping covers has to declare 404 — add it there, or move the mapping to the operations that do.

## controller-scope/pair-form-against-a-bodied-response
# the form check applies at controller scope too, which it did not before
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound) on 'GateController' maps to a 404 response that carries a body for 'opA', so a status alone cannot construct it. Supply one — @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound, { e in … }).

## controller-scope/closure-form-against-a-bare-response
# and in the other direction
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound, …) on 'GateController' supplies a body, but the document's 404 response carries none for 'opA'. Drop the closure.

## controller-scope/covered-operations-disagree-about-a-body
# the failure only controller scope can have: no form serves both, so the fix is to move the mapping rather than to change it
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound) on 'GateController' covers operations whose 404 responses disagree about carrying a body — with: 'opA'; without: 'opB'. One mapping cannot construct both — move it to route scope on each, or make the document agree.

## controller-scope/unconstructible-content-type
# reported before the pair/closure question, which has no right answer here
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound) on 'GateController' maps to a response whose content type this adapter cannot construct for 'opA' — it builds JSON bodies only. Use @RawOperation for those operations.

## ordering/catch-all-is-not-last
# a catch-all matches everything, so anything after it is dead
rejected: Controller.swift:12: error: @ErrorResponse(Swift.Error.self, .notFound) on 'opA' is a catch-all, so the mappings after it can never match — Gone. Put the catch-all last.

## accepted/per-operation-forms-are-the-remedy-for-disagreement
# each operation takes the form its own documented response requires
accepted
